definitions.explanation: Vinegar made from fermented rice, a fundamental seasoning in Japanese cuisine. It has a milder, slightly sweet flavor compared to Western grain or distilled vinegars, making it essential for sushi rice, dressings, and pickles.

examples.japanese: {米酢|こめず}で{酢|す}の{物|もの}を{作|つく}る。
examples.english: Make vinegared dishes with rice vinegar.

examples.japanese: {寿司|すし}には{米酢|こめず}が{欠|か}かせない。
examples.english: Rice vinegar is indispensable for sushi.

examples.japanese: {純|じゅん}{米酢|こめず}は{米|こめ}だけを{原料|げんりょう}にして{作|つく}られるので{風味|ふうみ}が{豊|ゆた}かだ。
examples.english: Pure rice vinegar is made solely from rice, so it has a rich flavor.

notes:
Compound of {米|こめ} ('rice') and {酢|す} ('vinegar'; voiced as ず in compounds). Also sometimes read as よねず. The most traditional and widely used vinegar in Japanese cooking.

TYPES:
- {純|じゅん}{米酢|こめず}: pure rice vinegar — made from 100% rice; richer flavor
- {穀物酢|こくもつす}: grain vinegar — made from mixed grains; cheaper and sharper
- {黒酢|くろず}: black vinegar — aged rice vinegar with a deeper, more complex flavor; popular as a health drink

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {米酢|こめず}を{使|つか}う: to use rice vinegar
- {米酢|こめず}で{味|あじ}をつける: to season with rice vinegar
- {米酢|こめず}と{砂糖|さとう}と{塩|しお}: rice vinegar, sugar, and salt (the classic sushi rice seasoning trio)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {穀物酢|こくもつす}: grain vinegar — made from a blend of grains; a cheaper, more pungent all-purpose vinegar
- {黒酢|くろず}: black vinegar — a dark, aged rice vinegar with a mellow, rich flavor
- {酢|す}: vinegar — the general term for all types of vinegar
- {寿司酢|すしず}: sushi vinegar — pre-mixed seasoned vinegar specifically for sushi rice, containing sugar and salt
